title: 第1196章 壳片的光第1195章 拼雾
lines: 雾团把第三缕散出去的雾丝收回来时，壳片上的纹路极轻极轻极轻地亮了一下。不是初火蓝那种光，是壳片本身的纹路在回应雾丝的触碰。
雾丝裹着茧膜的温度贴在壳片边缘，壳片震了震，纹路往虚空深处多延伸了一丝。
这一丝极细极细极细，细到几乎看不见，但雾团感应到了——壳片在帮它探。它裹着茧膜的核心还太小，收拢的雾丝还太少，够不到太远太远太远的地方。壳片的完整纹路能替它够。
拼碎片的人蹲在壳片旁边，碎片组成的手指轻轻按在壳片边缘。它看着壳片上的纹路延伸出去，光丝在它背后极轻极轻极轻地飘着。
“它在帮你。它以前是膜层刚冷却时自然脱落的第一片完整壳片。膜层把自己的一部分分给它，它从膜层上脱落的时候带走了膜层最完整的一段纹路。这段纹路能感应到和膜层同源的东西——你也是从膜层上脱落的，你散出去的雾丝也是膜层的一部分。它能帮你找到它们。”拼碎片的人的声音从不同碎片的光丝上渗出来，每个字都裹着极细微极细微极细微的颤，但颤法不一样了。以前是碎片的颤，现在是连贯的颤。
它的碎片与碎片之间的接缝在第一碎片的光里合拢成了纹路，说话的声音也在慢慢变连贯。
雾团把核心贴在壳片旁边。它学着壳片的方式把自己边缘的雾丝极轻极轻极轻地往前延伸——不是散，是探。散是被动的，飘到哪算哪。
探是主动的，沿着壳片纹路延伸的方向，极轻极轻极轻地往前触。触到极远极远极远处，有什么东西极轻极轻极轻地应了一下。
那是第四缕雾丝，飘得比前三缕更远更散更稀更薄更弱更怯更缓更慢更沉更古更老更未知。
它在极远处飘了很久很久很久，久到几乎和虚空融为一体。但壳片的纹路探过去时，它感应到了茧膜的温度——那是核心还在的温度。它开始往回飘。
拼碎片的人站起来，把壳片从碎片堆里轻轻拿起来，往前走了几步，放在更远处的另一片碎片上。
它说这里的碎片太稀，壳片放在这里能当锚点，雾团走过去的路上不会散。
它以前用光丝绑碎片时也是这样——光丝不够长，就先把最近的碎片绑住，再绑下一片。
壳片是完整的，比它的光丝更长更韧更稳，壳片能替雾团够到比它自己更远的地方。
卡拉斯站在不远处，看着拼碎片的人把壳片一片一片往前放，每放一次壳片的纹路就往更深处延伸一丝。它做了很久很久很久这种事——在边荒拼碎片，把碎掉的碎片一片一片接起来。
现在它在帮雾团把散掉的自己一片一片找回来。拼碎片和拼雾是同一种动作——接。
把碎掉的接起来，把散掉的收回来。它在边荒练了这么久这么久这么久的接，今天用在雾团身上，每放一次壳片就极轻极轻极轻地震一下，和它当年第一次用光丝把自己绑起来时一样的轻，一样的稳，一样的耐心。
雾团沿着壳片铺成的锚点往前走。它走得很慢，每走到一片壳片旁边就停下来，用茧膜的温度感应周围有没有散出去的雾丝。有就收回来，没有就继续往前走。
它从第一片壳片走到第三片壳片，收回了七缕雾丝。每一缕飘散的程度都不一样——有些只是飘到碎片间隙里，有些飘到极远极远极远处几乎感应不到。七缕雾丝从不同方向不同距离不同飘散程度极轻极轻极轻地飘回来，融进核心里。
核心比之前浓了不止一丝，边缘已经不再散了。它裹着茧膜的核心稳稳地停在壳片旁边，从只能保持极小极小极小的一团到能裹住自己、能走路、能探出边缘够到极远处的雾丝。
它用了很久很久很久才找回这些雾丝，但找回之后它就不再是那团只能蜷着等散的雾了。
拼碎片的人把壳片放在第五片碎片上。再往前更深处碎片更稀更薄更脆，壳片的纹路探过去时轻轻一颤——不是碰到雾丝，是碰到虚空里一片极薄极薄极薄的碎片。
这片碎片离雾团的核心很远很远很远，但它表面有什么东西在极轻极轻极轻地明灭。
壳片感应到了，把纹路收回来，在卡拉斯掌心轻轻震了一下。雾团停在第四片壳片旁边，核心极轻极轻极轻地一震。它也感应到了——不是雾丝，不是碎片本身，是碎片里裹着什么东西。
极古老极陌生极未知，被碎片裹着飘了太久太久太久，从来没被人碰过。拼碎片的人蹲下来，光丝在它背后极轻极轻极轻地飘着。
它说那不是雾丝，它拼了这么久，知道碎片的震波，知道雾的震波，但这股震波两者都不是。
是膜层刚形成时，还没有任何东西渗出去之前，封在膜层内部极深层极深层极深层的东西。
膜层后来冷却裂开分裂成亿万碎片，这东西就一直封在碎片里，从来没有暴露在外面。它比第一碎片更古老。
卡拉斯把壳片从碎片上拿起来，让壳片的纹路对准那片碎片的方向。他说先收雾丝，那个东西不急——它在碎片里封了这么久，不差这一会儿，先把雾团散出去的雾丝全收回来。
雾团把核心贴在壳片旁边，继续感应。它知道自己还没完整——还有些雾丝飘在更远更远更远处，它要把它们全找回来，然后再去看那片碎片里封着什么。
它从蜷着等散变成走着等收，收不回来的先放着，等收完雾丝它就能走到那片碎片面前，用茧膜的温度贴上去，告诉它：外面有人在。
它等了这么久，等的不是被人破开，是有人告诉它外面还在。
content_en:
When the fog brought back the third wisp of mist, the lines on the shell shone very lightly. It's not the light of the early fire blue, it's the texture of the shell itself responding to the touch of the mist thread.
The warmth of the mist silk wrapped in the cocoon film stuck to the edge of the shell. The shell shook, and the lines extended a little deeper into the void.
This trace was extremely thin, so thin that it was almost invisible, but the mist sensed it - the shell pieces were helping it detect. Its cocoon-coated core is still too small, and the gathered mist threads are still too few, so it cannot reach too far or too far. The complete texture of the shell pieces can be enough for it.
The person piecing together the pieces squatted next to the shell piece, and his fingers composed of pieces gently pressed against the edge of the shell piece. It watched the lines on the shell extend out, and the light threads floated very lightly behind it.
"It's helping you. It used to be the first complete shell piece that naturally fell off when the film layer just cooled. The film layer gave it a part of itself, and when it fell off from the film layer, it took away the most complete texture of the film layer. This texture can sense things that have the same origin as the film layer - You are also detached from the film layer, and the mist fibers you disperse are also part of the film layer. It can help you find them." The voice of the person who pieced together the fragments seeped out from the light filaments of different fragments, and each word was wrapped in a very tiny, tiny, tiny tremor, but the trembling method was different. It used to be a fragmented tremor, but now it is a coherent tremor.
The seams between its fragments closed into lines in the light of the first fragment, and the voice slowly became coherent.
The fog sticks the core next to the shell pieces. It imitates the method of shell pieces and extends the mist threads on its edge very lightly and very lightly forward - not spreading, but exploring. Dispersion is passive, and it doesn't matter where it floats.
The probe is active, touching forward very lightly, very lightly, along the direction in which the shell lines extend. Touching very far away, something responded very lightly.
That was the fourth wisp of mist, which floated further than the first three wisps, was more diffuse, thinner, weaker, timid, slow, heavy, ancient, older, and unknown.
It floated in the distance for a long, long, long time, until it almost merged with the void. But when the lines of the shell probed through, it sensed the temperature of the cocoon membrane—the temperature at which the core was still there. It started to float back.
The person who was piecing together the fragments stood up, gently picked up the shell fragment from the pile of fragments, took a few steps forward, and placed it on another fragment farther away.
It said that the fragments here were too thin and that the shell fragments could be used as anchor points so that the fog would not disperse as it walked over.
It used to be like this when tying fragments with light wire - the light thread was not long enough, so it tied the nearest fragment first, and then tied the next piece.
The shell piece is complete, longer, tougher and more stable than its light filament. The shell piece can reach farther than itself for the fog mass.
Karas stood not far away, watching the people who put the pieces together put the shell pieces forward one by one, and the lines of the shell pieces extended a little deeper every time they were placed. It has been doing this for a long, long time - piecing together pieces in the wilderness and connecting the broken pieces piece by piece.
Now it is helping the mist to retrieve the scattered pieces of itself piece by piece. Piecing together fragments and piecing together mist are the same action - pick up.
Pick up what is broken and take back what is scattered. It has been practicing binding in the wilderness for so long, and today it is used on Wu Tuan. Every time it puts the shell piece, it shakes very lightly. It is as light, stable and patient as when it first tied itself up with light silk.
The fog moves forward along the anchor points made of shell flakes. It walked very slowly, stopping every time it came to a piece of shell, using the temperature of its cocoon membrane to sense whether there were any loose threads of mist around it. If you have it, take it back, if not, keep moving forward.
It walked from the first shell piece to the third shell piece and retracted seven wisps of mist. The degree of dispersion of each wisp is different - some just float into the gaps between the debris, and some float so far away that they are almost undetectable. Seven wisps of mist floated back from different directions, distances, and degrees, and merged into the core.
The core is more than a little thicker than before, and the edges are no longer loose. Its cocoon-wrapped core rests steadily next to the shell pieces, from being able to remain only a tiny, tiny ball to a mist thread that can wrap itself around, walk, and poke out the edge to reach extremely far away.
It took it a long, long, long time to retrieve these mist threads, but after retrieval, it was no longer the mist that could only curl up and wait to disperse.
The person putting the pieces together places the shell piece on top of the fifth piece. Going deeper, the fragments became thinner, thinner, and brittle. The shell's lines trembled slightly when it was explored - not when it encountered mist threads, but when it encountered an extremely thin, extremely thin, extremely thin fragment in the void.
This fragment was far, far, far away from the core of the fog, but something on its surface was flickering on and off very lightly.
The shell sensed it, retracted the lines, and lightly vibrated in Karas's palm. The mist stopped next to the fourth shell piece, and the core shook very lightly. It also sensed it - not the mist, not the fragments themselves, but something wrapped in the fragments.
Extremely ancient, extremely strange, and unknown. It has been wrapped in debris and floated for too long, too long, and has never been touched by anyone. The person who was piecing together the pieces squatted down, and the light thread floated very lightly behind it.
It said that it was not mist silk. It had been fighting for so long and knew the shock wave of fragments and the mist shock wave, but this shock wave was neither.
It is something that is sealed very deep inside the film when it is first formed and before anything seeps out.
The film later cooled and cracked and split into billions of fragments. This thing has been sealed in the fragments and has never been exposed to the outside. It is older than the First Shard.
Karas lifted the shell piece from the fragment, aligning its lines with the fragment. He said that he should collect the fog thread first. There is no need to worry about that thing - it has been sealed in the debris for so long, so it is not bad.
title_en: Chapter 1196 The Light of the Shell Chapter 1195 Fighting the Fog
